1.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh gives Ezekiel his message to Gog.

God calls Ezekiel this to emphasize that Ezekiel is only a human being. God is eternal and powerful, but humans are not. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [mortal person] or [human]
This tells the reader to pay special attention to what follows. Alternate translation: [Look!] or [Listen!] or [Pay attention to what I am about to tell you!]

Some modern versions interpret the Hebrew expression as “prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal.” This is another title for Gog. See how you translated these names in Ezekiel 38:2. Alternate translation: [who is the prince of Meshech and Tubal]

2.q: I will turn you and lead you on
2.note: God speaks of leading Gog as if Gog was an animal.
God speaks of bringing Gog “up” to Israel because it was located in the mountains.

3.q: I will knock your bow out of your left hand and make the arrows fall from your right hand.
3.note: Knocking Gog’s bow and arrows out of his hands is spoken of as if God is destroying Gog’s military power.

4.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh continues giving Ezekiel his message to Gog.
These refer to the same people. It can be stated as a single phrase. Alternate translation: [all your soldiers]

4.q: I will give you to the birds of prey and the wild beasts of the fields for food
4.note: The scavengers eating the corpses is spoken of as if Yahweh was giving food to them.

5.q: this is the Lord Yahweh’s declaration
5.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared]

6.q: I will send out fire on Magog
6.note: This could mean: (1) Yahweh will send literal fire down on Gog and his army or (2) “fire” is a metonym for the destruction that it causes.
This is the name of an ancient nation that probably lived in the land that is now Turkey. Magog might be the ancient nation of Lydia. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 38:2.

When Yahweh says that people will know that he is Yahweh, he is implying that they will know that he is the one true God who has supreme authority and power. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 6:7. Alternate translation: [understand that I am Yahweh, the one true God] or [realize that I, Yahweh, have supreme power and authority]

7.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh continues giving Ezekiel his message to Gog.

7.q: I will make my holy name known in the midst of my people Israel
7.note: Here the metonym “my holy name” refers to Yahweh’s character. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will make my people, Israel, know that I am holy] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

8.note: This tells the reader to pay special attention to what follows. Alternate translation: [Look!] or [Listen!] or [Pay attention to what I am about to tell you!]
These two phrases have similar meaning and emphasize the fact that this will really happen. Alternate translation: [is surely going to happen]

9.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh continues giving Ezekiel his message to Gog.
These two phrases mean the same thing. The Israelites will use the wood from the weapons as kindling for fires. Alternate translation: [to start fires]

9.q: small shields, large shields, bows, arrows, the clubs and spears
9.note: This list includes all the typical weapons of war of that day. It may represent weapons in general.
wooden sticks used as a weapon

10.q: wanted to take … wanted to plunder
10.note: Here “to take” and “to plunder” mean the same thing. Gog intended to take Israel’s possessions, but Yahweh prevented him so that he was not able to do that.

11.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh begins to tell Ezekiel what will happen to Gog.

11.q: it will happen on that day that
11.note: This signals an important event. If your language has a way for doing this, you could use it here.

11.q: to the east of the sea
11.note: A few modern versions interpret the Hebrew expression here as “to the east toward the sea.”
This could mean: (1) “The grave will block” or (2) “The dead army will block.”
Alternate translation: [There the house of Israel]
Alternate translation: [Valley of the Great Army of Gog]

12.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh continues to tell Ezekiel what will happen to Gog.

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelites] or [the Israelite people group]

12.q: will bury them in order to purify the land
12.note: In Jewish law, a dead body defiled anything it touched and made it “unclean.” Burying these bodies is spoken of as cleansing or purifying the land.
Alternate translation: [bury the soldiers of Gog’s army]

13.q: this is the Lord Yahweh’s declaration
13.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared]

14.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh continues to tell Ezekiel what will happen to Gog.
Alternate translation: [through the land of Israel]

14.q: those who were traveling through, but who died and their bodies remained on the surface of the land
14.note: This refers to the dead bodies of Gog’s soldiers whom Yahweh killed as they entered the land.

14.q: so that they may bury them
14.note: Alternate translation: [so that the designated men may bury the dead bodies]
In Jewish law, a dead body defiled anything it touched and made it “unclean.” Burying these bodies is spoken of as cleansing or purifying the land. (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))
This “seventh” is the ordinal number for seven.

15.note: Bones would be all that remained of the corpses after a period of time.

15.q: they will put a marker by it, until gravediggers come and bury it
15.note: There are apparently two groups of men. The first will mark the location of corpses, and the second group will bury them.

16.note: In Jewish law, a dead body defiled anything it touched and made it “unclean.” Burying these bodies is spoken of as cleansing or purifying the land. (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

17.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh gives Ezekiel a message for the birds and the wild animals about what they will do to Gog.

God calls Ezekiel this to emphasize that Ezekiel is only a human being. God is eternal and powerful, but humans are not. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [mortal person] or [human]
“to the feast” or “to the slaughter.” Yahweh means that he will give the birds and animals a very good meal and not that he is worshiping them.

18.q: they will be rams, lambs, goats, and bulls
18.note: Yahweh is speaking with irony. Normally people sacrificed animals to God. Here, God is sacrificing people to animals. Alternate translation: [as if they were male sheep, lambs, goats, and bulls]

18.q: they were all fattened in Bashan
18.note: That can be stated in active form. Alternate translation: [they all became fat while grazing in Bashan]

19.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh continues to give Ezekiel a message for the birds and the wild animals about what they will do to Gog.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **satisfaction**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [until you are satisfied]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **drunkenness**, you can express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: [until you become drunk] or [until you are intoxicated]

20.note: The metonym “chariot” refers to the men in the chariots. Alternate translation: [chariot driver]

20.q: this is the Lord Yahweh’s declaration
20.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared]

21.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh gives Ezekiel a message about what will happen to Israel.

21.q: I will set my glory among the nations
21.note: Yahweh speaks of his glory as if he will place it in the middle of the nations where they can see it. Alternate translation: [I will make the nations see my glory]

21.q: my judgment that I perform and my hand that I have set against them
21.note: Both of these phrases refer to the punishment that Yahweh will inflict upon Israel and are repeated for emphasis. They can be combined into a single phrase. Alternate translation: [the way that I will judge them]
Here the metonym “hand” refers to Yahweh’s power that he uses to bring punishment.
Alternate translation: [against Gog and his great army]

22.note: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelites] or [the Israelite people group]

23.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh continues to give Ezekiel a message about what will happen to Israel.

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelites] or [the Israelite people group]

23.q: because of their iniquity by which they betrayed me
23.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **iniquity**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [because they sinned and betrayed me]

23.q: I hid my face from them
23.note: Here “face” refers to Yahweh’s help and protection. Alternate translation: [I stopped protecting them and taking care of them]

23.q: gave them into the hand of their adversaries
23.note: Here the metonym “hand” refers to power. Alternate translation: [gave their enemies power over them]

23.q: all of them fell by the sword
23.note: Here falling represents being killed, and the sword represents battle. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 32:23. Alternate translation: [their enemies killed them all in battle]

24.note: This speaks of the people’s disgusting behavior as if they were physically unclean. Here “uncleanness” means basically the same as “sins.” Alternate translation: [their disgusting behavior and their sins] or [their sins] (See also: [Doublet](ta:figs-doublet))

25.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh continues to give Ezekiel a message about what will happen to Israel.

25.q: will restore the fortunes of Jacob
25.note: Translate “will restore the fortunes” as in Ezekiel 16:53. However, some modern versions interpret the Hebrew expression here as “will bring Jacob back from captivity.”

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelites] or [the Israelite people group]

25.q: act with zeal for my holy name
25.note: Alternate translation: [make sure that they honor me]

26.q: they will bear their shame and all the treason
26.note: Experts do not agree on the meaning of this phrase. This could mean: (1) “they will regret their shame and all the treason” or (2) “they will forget their shame and all the treason.”

27.q: I will show myself to be holy in the sight of many nations
27.note: Here “sight” is a metonym for understanding. Alternate translation: [many nations will understand that I am holy because of what I did for the house of Israel]

28.note:
# Connecting Statement:

Yahweh continues to give Ezekiel a message about what will happen to Israel.

28.q: I sent them into captivity … I will gather them back to their land
28.note: At the time when Ezekiel wrote, Israel was still in captivity in Babylon.

29.q: I will no longer hide my face from them
29.note: Here “no longer hide my face” is an idiom that means Yahweh will not continue to abandon Israel to exile in Babylon. Alternate translation: [I will no longer abandon them]

29.q: when I pour out my Spirit on the house of Israel
29.note: Here to give the Spirit abundantly is spoken of as to “pour out” the Spirit. Alternate translation: [when I generously give my Spirit to the house of Israel]

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelites] or [the Israelite people group]

29.q: this is the Lord Yahweh’s declaration
29.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared]
